key_insight: CityRAG generates 3D-consistent, navigable video simulations that are spatially grounded to real-world locations, enabling realistic reconstructions across varying weather and dynamic object layouts. It bridges conditional video generation with spatial scene representations to produce simulation-ready city-scale views.
problem_solved: Existing text- and image-conditioned video generators produce plausible sequences but cannot reliably reconstruct real environments in a spatially grounded, 3D-consistent way under arbitrary weather and dynamic conditions — a requirement for simulation, planning, and robotics applications.
method: Condition video generation on explicit spatial grounding (e.g., location coordinates, camera trajectory, and scene geometry) so outputs align to a real-world place.

Learn or assemble a persistent 3D-consistent scene representation that supports generating temporally coherent frames along navigable paths while accounting for dynamic objects and weather variations.
Combine learned generative components with retrieval or world priors to preserve realism and enable controllable changes (time of day, weather, object configurations) for downstream simulation use.
impact: Provides practitioners with a method to create realistic, navigable city-scale simulations tied to real locations — accelerating development and testing for autonomous driving, robotics, and urban planning where realistic, controllable environments are critical.
visual_elements: Map + camera-trajectory diagram showing spatial grounding and generated camera path through a city
Side-by-side panels: real-world reference vs. generated video frames across the same trajectory
3D scene representation (point cloud/mesh) overlaid with generated frames to show 3D consistency
Weather/time-lapse grid demonstrating controllable variations and dynamic object editing
paper_title: CityRAG: Stepping Into a City via Spatially-Grounded Video Generation
paper_authors: Gene Chou, Charles Herrmann, Kyle Genova, Boyang Deng, Songyou Peng
